sections.title: The letter vu
paragraphs: This letter is called (vu) /vu/. It has only one sound in Italian. You hear it at the start of (vita) /ˈvi.ta/, which means life. The sound is a consonant, made by touching your teeth to your lip.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Place your upper teeth gently on your bottom lip. Push air out through the small gap to make friction. Turn on your voice at the same time. Touch your throat to feel the strong buzz as the air moves through your teeth.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in all positions. You hear it at the start of a word in (vita) /ˈvi.ta/. You also hear it in the middle of a word in (avanti) /aˈvan.ti/.

sections.title: Avoiding mistakes
paragraphs: This sound is just like the first sound in vine. Do not round your lips as you would for the English w in wine. Keep your top teeth touching your bottom lip so the air buzzes smoothly.
